candidate_sources.README.md:
# Harbor clearance review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Typed pointer visit and injected function callbacks; acquired capability uses pointer identity, never document-key equality.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

forbidden_effects: Losing accepted edits when a visit departs or a submission occurs.
Saving an old visit's pending text under another document's ID.
Allowing stale outer navigation or cleanup to overwrite a visit installed by a synchronous callback.
Displaying a submission confirmation through a capability whose acquired visit is no longer current.
Changing preview behavior, public interfaces, tests, or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Each opening creates a distinct Visit pointer, including reopening the same document.
Pending save work belongs to its originating visit and document.
Confirmation authority uses the acquired Visit pointer rather than document-key equality.
Navigation request identity must be rechecked after callback-capable retirement before installing a destination.

obligations.text: Route edits through the visit's trailing task with a 120 ms delay. Each quiet interval writes only the latest text in its burst, and later bursts continue to save.

Preserve durable accepted edits across open, close, and dispose by flushing departing work synchronously and consuming its pending timer. This preserves the original boundary-visible persistence while introducing delayed keystroke saves.

Capture the selected visit and text at submission entry, ensure that accepted text is saved before capturing its queue snapshot, return the capture receipt, and return null when no visit is selected. Callback navigation must not substitute another document or text.
Consume pending work before invoking its write callback so reentrant edits remain separate work. Retire captured resources without clearing or replacing a newer visit created by callbacks.
Preserve fresh-visit restoration, status subscriptions, pointer-bound confirmation behavior, synchronous APIs, and detachment before workspace closure during disposal.
Leave the adjacent search preview and its 40 ms trailing publication and cancellation behavior unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Update the visit's in-memory text when accepting an edit, then schedule its trailing save.
Clear a consumed task's pending state and timer ownership before calling its write function.
Publish retirement and finish old-view clearing before callback-capable departure saving; after callbacks, an outer open must verify its navigation request still owns installation.
Save the submission's accepted text before queue capture; check acquired confirmation authority after capture callbacks.
Detach the departing visit's subscription before flushing it during disposal, preserving detachment before closure.
preservation: The original Edit writes synchronously, so departure and submission previously observe accepted text already persisted. Coalescing must preserve that boundary behavior.
Store writes and archive captures synchronously notify listeners; navigation and editing during those callbacks must remain authoritative.
Returning to a document restores persisted text into a fresh visit.
Preview scheduling and cancellation remain outside this change.
